spatial_claims.claim: Pyramid ABCD has triangular base ABC and vertex D; pyramid EFGH has triangular base EFG and vertex H; both pyramids have the same height h.
K, L, M are midpoints of AB, AC, AD respectively; N, O, P are midpoints of BC, BD, CD respectively. Prisms have triangular cross-sections determined by these midpoints.
The two prisms from ABCD each have the same height as the two prisms from EFGH because the subdivision bisects the height uniformly for both pyramids.
A prism on a triangular base equals half the parallelepiped on the same base and height; prisms of equal height are to one another as their bases.
The base of the prism from ABCD is the medial triangle of ABC (formed by joining midpoints of sides), which has area one-fourth that of triangle ABC. Similarly for EFGH.

The two smaller pyramids from each original pyramid are equal, similar to each other and to the original. Corresponding sub-pyramids from ABCD and EFGH have the same height because the subdivision halves the height uniformly.
Bases of smaller pyramids from ABCD are similar to ABC and have area one-fourth of the parent triangle. The same ratio ABC:EFG is maintained at every subdivision level.

configuration_map: Pyramid ABCD: base triangle ABC in a plane, vertex D above at height h. Midpoints K(AB), L(AC), M(AD), N(BC), O(BD), P(CD). The 12.3 construction produces two equal prisms (one with medial triangle KLN as base, area = (1/4)ABC; one with parallelogram base, equal in volume) and two smaller similar pyramids each with linear scale 1/2, height h/2, and base area (1/4)ABC. Pyramid EFGH: analogous construction with same height h, producing corresponding prisms and sub-pyramids with matching heights at every level. At each recursive subdivision level, all corresponding sub-pyramids from ABCD and EFGH have equal heights (h/2^n at level n), and all prism base ratios reduce to ABC:EFG.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof is a proportional argument about prisms from recursive pyramid subdivision. The spatial claims (equal heights preserved by uniform halving, midpoint constructions producing medial triangles with 1/4 area, similar sub-pyramids maintaining the base ratio) are all compatible. There are no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior point conflicts, and no ray ordering issues. Each height, area, and similarity claim follows correctly from the established 3D configuration.
